raw_response:
I am not changing much this year. My land is only 10.7 mu, and money must be spent carefully. I have farmed this wheat-maize land many years, so I will do it the usual way: wheat first, then maize right after. If I gamble and cut fertilizer too much, yield can fall badly. But I also cannot spend like the big farmers. So I will use a middle amount, same as what has worked on my fields and what people around me do. We have a well, so for wheat I will give water at the key times if the ground is dry. Maize depends more on rain, but if it turns dry after sowing or around tasseling, I will pump once. Family labor is limited because some people work outside, so I will keep the work simple and use machine service for harvest and sowing when needed.

For wheat, I will sow in early October after maize comes off. I usually buy ordinary local improved seed from the dealer in town, not expensive fancy seed. Before sowing I will put one base fertilizer, then later if the wheat does not look strong I will topdress once around jointing. Wheat cannot miss water at the important stages, so I plan around three irrigations if the year is normal. After wheat harvest in June, there is no time to waste. I will clear the field fast, do light tillage or direct sow if the machine comes in time, and plant maize right away. For maize I will buy hybrid seed because that gives steadier ears. I will put some fertilizer at sowing and another little bit before the big growth stage. Usually maize here follows the rain, so I do not plan much irrigation unless the season turns dry. This way I keep grain coming from both crops and do not leave myself short of cash.
